claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation will improve the wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix.
The proposed architecture is analogous to the nanohierarchical, composition-undulated architecture used in Ni50(AlNbTiV)50.
The intervention creates a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Wear protection is governed by intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The nanohierarchical structure provides multiple types of adaptive friction-interface protection.
The cooperative nanostructure releases gradient frictional stress during wear.
The architecture activates a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer during high-temperature wear.
The proposed mechanisms will improve the wear resistance of the modified FeNiCrCoCu coating relative to the unchanged coating under identical conditions.
The intervention may reduce wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from room temperature to 800 °C.
The prediction applies from low to high friction velocities.
The prediction applies from shallow to deep wear depths.
The exact wear-improvement mechanism and the optimal composition and architecture remain uncertain.
Modified and unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coatings will be compared under identical sliding conditions while temperature, velocity, and wear depth are varied.
The experiment will measure wear rate, friction coefficient, and microscopic deformation behavior.
Failure of the modified coating to achieve a significantly lower wear rate than the unchanged coating will falsify the hypothesis.
